problem:

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y \\ (x-y)^{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$

the total derivative $\boldsymbol f'$ is given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/5b729806def4b82ee72cd58bc41f39ceb2d1acad82d3a7098fec5bc6be925d6b.png)
From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
examples.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/0496b786dfda2338d951906d6fafb261e9aee95d9390423e69a5a55a76790918.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/bb37d8fdb7e4da90a22933c264d49ff999a3502618a6cd3725e8a5a2fd55a9ed.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/f2c5b815b56c791d1538c225c954c2fdc5603f879e4254838bb73994b6493d48.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})=2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{y}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/238be519e096397dafb2ad5b915d07a09f5129dc897b45955715e76da1146d1e.png)
Thus, the missing entries are $y,\:$ $0,\:$ and $\ln{x}.$

feedback.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}+{y}^{3},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3})=2x, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3})=3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}2(2) & 3(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
